claims.statement: To discover an internal board ID, `get_board_id` uses a cached value or inspects Open list 1, then falls back to nonempty lists when Open has no cards, and caches the discovered ID.
Reminder creation posts a card reminder payload with type 1 and card_type 0, while stopping working-on requires the working-on record ID rather than the card ID.

CLI, TUI, and MCP surfaces all delegate card and comment mutations to shared `operations` helpers over `HteamClient`; CLI commands create a `Session` first so authentication is available before card workflows run.

Board resolution follows an explicit override, then the configured board, then the last saved board, and switching the active board clears the cached internal board ID before later mutations resolve it again.

Card creation resolves board ID, board number, and user ID, sends a JSON payload with `name`, `complement`, `process`, and optional `labels`, and falls back to a name lookup or an ID-zero success-shaped card when the create response is empty, invalid, or unusable.

The shared move operation defaults an omitted source list to `1` (Open), while the TUI supplies its explicit source list during optimistic moves so rollback can restore the card to the correct original list and index.

Full card updates fetch current detail, GET the HTML edit form, merge the form baseline with any patch, and POST an encoded full form; omitted fields are preserved by preferring current detail or baseline values, while priority defaults to `3` if neither source provides it.

`TaskEditFormBaseline` and `merge_edit_form_into_detail` act as the preservation boundary for edit-form-only fields: priority from the form is merged back into `CardDetail`, and a nonblank form `time_estimated` fills a missing detail value.

Close and reopen are dedicated task-lifecycle POSTs, not list moves; when no family override is supplied, the operation resolves the task family from `title_url` and then calls the matching `close/` or `reopen/` endpoint.
Comment date input uses `COMMENT_DATE_FORMAT`; blank or omitted input becomes the current local time, while supplied input is strictly parsed before the comment is posted.

Posting a comment first loads the task page to extract `timestamp`, `security_hash`, and CSRF form tokens, then submits an URL-encoded form containing the task, reply target, honeypot, comment text, optional follow flag, and date; HTTP statuses below `400` count as success.

TUI comment composition rejects blank text, clears compose state after a successful post, refreshes comments when possible without converting a successful post into a failure, and preserves the composer state when the post itself fails.
Mention completion only inspects the trailing whitespace-delimited token, requests suggestions even for a bare `@`, and replaces an accepted partial mention with `@username `.

The TUI refreshes cards or working state after successful creation or toggling, but preserves the previous visible state when those follow-up refreshes fail so a nonfatal reload does not erase accepted mutations.

Focused tests cover list and card decoding, source-list defaults, family-specific close and reopen, detail-plus-edit updates, comment date and mention behavior, reminder payloads, working start/stop behavior, and required comment form tokens.
CLI card commands open a Session before calling operations, and the session refuses to construct a client unless authentication is present.
CLI, TUI, and MCP all route card mutations through shared operations helpers rather than calling HteamClient directly from the adapters.
Board selection uses explicit board first, then configured board, then the last board saved by the TUI or board-switch flow, and missing board values are treated as errors when a board is required.
`create_card` depends on both a board number and an internal board ID, with `get_board_id` using an in-memory cache first and falling back to probing list 1 or scanning lists with cards when needed.
The shared `move_card` operation defaults an omitted source list to 1 (Open), which is convenient for CLI and MCP callers but unsafe when the card is known to be in another list.

`move_card` posts JSON to `boards/care/labels/update_card_position/` with board_id, card_id, from_list, to_list, and card_type 0, and any 2xx response counts as success while failures preserve the response body in the error.
The TUI performs card moves optimistically and rolls back the local list ordering if the remote move fails.
Close and reopen are dedicated task-lifecycle calls that resolve the task family from title_url unless the caller overrides it, and they do not move cards between lists.
`update-desc` is a narrow write, while the broader update workflow fetches current task detail and then posts a full edit form so omitted fields survive the round trip.
The HTML task edit form is the source of truth for partial updates because task JSON often omits or reshapes editable fields such as dependence, priority, time_estimated, start_date, and responsible.
After posting a full edit form, the client treats a response that still looks like the edit page as a failure even if the HTTP status is 200.

Comments are posted through a site-side HTML form: the client fetches the task page, extracts timestamp, security_hash, and CSRF, then URL-encodes and submits the form with content_type=processes.task, object_pk, reply_to, comment text, and date.
Comment date parsing is strict on `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, while a blank or omitted date defaults to the current local time rather than UTC.
`follow` is optional in comment posting and is sent as `follow=on` only when true; MCP defaults an absent optional field to false.
The TUI comment workflow rejects whitespace-only text, clears composer state after a successful post, and keeps the successful post even if the follow-up comment refresh fails.
The comment mention helper only treats the trailing whitespace-delimited token as a potential `@` mention query, and a bare `@` produces an empty query so suggestions appear immediately.
The TUI comment composer requests username suggestions on each qualifying keystroke without debounce and replaces the trailing partial token with the selected mention text.

Dates and time mutations are separate board-card AJAX routes that resolve the internal board_id before writing, validate their inputs, and return the resolved board ID so callers can report the touched board-card route.
Working-on status is independent of card placement, and start/stop operations normalize empty, array, or singleton responses while stop uses the working record ID rather than the card ID.

The TUI refreshes after successful mutations where appropriate, including reloading the target list after new-card creation and attempting popup reloads for comment and reminder actions without converting reload failures into mutation failures.

Focused tests cover board ID extraction, Open-list defaulting for moves, family resolution for close and reopen, full-update form posting, comment token extraction, strict date validation, mention-token rules, reminder payloads, and working-on record lookup.
Reply targets are carried by `reply_to`, which is optional in the comment form and defaults to `0` when omitted.
Scheduled follow-ups are keyed by the follow-up record ID embedded in the task page, and completing or canceling one posts only CSRF to `/followup/{id}/complete` or `/followup/{id}/cancel`.

The mention helper only inspects the trailing whitespace-delimited token, so only a trailing unfinished `@` token can trigger suggestions; a bare `@` yields an empty query and still requests usernames immediately.
The TUI comment autocomplete requests suggestions on each qualifying keystroke without debounce and replaces the trailing partial mention with `@selected_text `.

The TUI comment workflow clears the compose state after a successful post, attempts to refresh comments without turning a refresh failure into a failed post, and preserves the composer state when the post itself fails.
The follow-up parser keeps the follow-up record ID, associated comment ID, and locale-formatted date text from the task page rather than trying to normalize the date string.
Full card updates use the HTML edit form as the preservation boundary, because task JSON often omits or reshapes fields such as dependence, priority, time_estimated, start_date, and responsible.

The HTML edit form baseline lets `update_card_full` preserve sibling fields from the existing form while posting a merged full form, and `merge_edit_form_into_detail` rehydrates priority and time estimate back into `CardDetail` for display after refresh.

Comment posting first fetches the task page to extract `timestamp`, `security_hash`, and CSRF tokens, then submits an URL-encoded form with `content_type=processes.task`, `object_pk`, `reply_to`, `comment`, optional `follow=on`, and `date`; any HTTP status below 400 counts as success.
`follow` is optional in comment posting and is serialized as `follow=on` only when true; the CLI, MCP, and TUI set or default it to false unless explicitly enabled.

Creation can return an empty body, invalid JSON, or a decoded card with ID `0`; in those cases the client falls back to a name lookup in the target list or returns a minimal success-shaped card with ID `0` and the requested name.

The shared move operation posts JSON to `boards/care/labels/update_card_position/` with board number, card ID, source list, destination list, and `card_type: 0`, and treats any 2xx response as success while preserving failure bodies in errors.
The TUI performs optimistic moves and restores the original list ordering if the remote move fails.
Close and reopen are dedicated task-lifecycle calls that resolve the task family from `title_url` unless the caller overrides it, and they do not move cards between lists.
The board-family resolution logic prefers an explicit board, then the configured board, then the last saved board, and a missing board becomes an error when a board is required.
`get_board_id` first uses its cache, then probes list 1, then scans nonempty lists until it finds an internal board ID, and caches the result for later mutations.
`create_card` depends on both a board number and an internal board ID, and `get_board_id` feeds that requirement through the cached-or-probed resolution path.

Dates and time mutations are separate board-card AJAX routes that resolve the internal board_id before writing, validate their inputs, and return the resolved board ID so callers can report the touched route.
